sentences.text: Warren Arter used his position - running a unit investigating sexual assaults in south-east London - to target women it was his job to protect.

sentences.text: Two women, speaking out for the first time, have told Panorama how Arter groomed them.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: In the case of his wife, Rebekah, he filmed her being sexually abused and distributed the footage.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: She died in Barbados two years ago, while on holiday with him.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: On Sunday, the BBC revealed how he lied about what happened on the Caribbean island.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: There were multiple investigations into Arter while he was employed by the Met.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Now the former detective who led one of them has told the BBC that senior bosses tried to interfere with his inquiries, despite him having found potential victims.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: While Arter was suspended as a result of that investigation, he remained on full pay for seven years - before being sacked in 2023 for drug offences.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: The following year, the Met - having learned of his wife's death in Barbados - arrested him on his return to the UK for sexual offences alleged by another woman.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Arter took his own life days later in HMP Wandsworth.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Despite the evidence against him, the Met has not reviewed all the cases he handled.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Arter subjected his wife, Rebekah, to years of abuse In response to our investigation, the Metropolitan Police has for the first time publicly apologised to the women he abused.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: It said it was now working to examine Arter's electronic devices to identify if there are further victims and that it encouraged other women to come forward.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Panorama has uncovered several opportunities to stop Arter that were missed by the Met: In 2010, medical staff found Arter alone with a woman in the toilets of a sexual assault referral centre hours after she had reported being raped.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Panorama can now reveal that 21 potential victims of Arter were identified in an investigation by the police watchdog, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC).
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: The Met has not contacted all the women whose cases he investigated during his 20 years as a serving officer.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: The upskirting image that was sent in March 2024 to a woman we are calling Layla should have led to Arter's arrest.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Bail conditions or custody would have prevented him from taking his wife, Rebekah, to Barbados.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: On 28 June, Arter rang Rebekah's relatives from the island to tell them she had died.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Rebekah had been escaping an abusive relationship in 2006 when the Met put then-Det Sgt Warren Arter in charge of investigating her former partner.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Arter pursued Rebekah, they began a relationship and he quickly moved in with her.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Her now-adult son, Elliot, says Arter initially made his mum feel "safer" but that his behaviour soon changed.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: "He'd say to her: 'Get in the kitchen, make my dinner you slag.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Make me a tea you [expletive] bitch,'" Elliot recalls.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Arter would openly watch pornography on his tablet while he was in the living room with her, Elliot says.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: He also collected urine from Elliot, claiming he was testing it at the police lab to help the boy's promising football career - but Elliot now suspects it was an effort to hide Arter's drug use.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: The Predator in the Police Warren Arter was seen as a star detective in the Metropolitan Police, but he was also a sexual predator.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Why didn't the Met act sooner to stop the predator in its ranks?
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: In the years before she died, Arter had filmed and distributed videos of his wife being sexually abused.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: The BBC has seen some of them.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Many show her unconscious or otherwise incapacitated while Arter insults her.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: "You should get raped," he says, in one video.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: In another, Arter can be heard speaking to a man behind the camera, asking him to be quiet and saying "they go mad otherwise" - suggesting the video was being made for a wider audience.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: His crimes were so brazen that he sent abuse videos of Rebekah unsolicited to at least four women he knew.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Two were women whose cases he had investigated - one of them was Layla.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: She had met Arter in 2010 after she reported being raped.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: His exploitation of her continued for more than a decade, up until she reported the upskirting image - which she had deleted - to staff from the IOPC.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Both Layla, and her adult daughter who was with her when she spoke to the IOPC, say she identified the woman in the photo as Rebekah - whom she recognised from previous videos.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: The IOPC says the staff member has no record or recollection of being told the identity of the woman in the photo - and it did not have the authority to investigate as Arter was no longer a police officer.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: It did, however, tell the Metropolitan Police about the upskirting allegation.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Arter's abuse could have been stopped more than a decade earlier - soon after he had met Rebekah.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: He claimed their relationship had begun after a chance meeting on a night out, an account she corroborated, when he was questioned by the IOPC during an investigation started in 2017.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: However, Panorama has learned Rebekah was bombarded with more than nine hours of calls from Met phone numbers in the three months following the conclusion of her case in 2006.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: We also know that Arter searched her name on Met computer systems without any obvious justification.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Officers have faced misconduct proceedings, even prison, for relationships which began in similar circumstances, but at that time Arter was not disciplined.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: Arter falsely claimed he had met Rebekah by chance on a night out It is not clear when his bosses found out about the relationship, but some of his colleagues appear to have known early on.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: The BBC understands that four officers told the IOPC investigation they believed Arter had met Rebekah on a case.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: One said they knew Rebekah had been a victim of domestic abuse, but they refused to sign a statement.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: The Met told Panorama that the IOPC's subsequent report had found that Arter's colleagues knew of his relationship with Rebekah, but did not know he had met her in the course of his duties, therefore he was not subject to any misconduct proceedings.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: None of the various investigations into Arter led to criminal charges before he was arrested in 2024.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: On one occasion, he even received a payout after being arrested for harassment.
sentences.article_title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women

sentences.text: The IOPC has now told the BBC that of 21 possible Arter victims it had identified by 2020, it assessed he had inappropriate contact or relationships with eight of them, including Layla and Rebekah.

sentences.text: Panorama has, however, learned of at least one more alleged victim who says she was groomed and sexually exploited over 12 years.

sentences.text: Former Victims' Commissioner for England and Wales, Dame Vera Baird, is calling for an investigation by an outside force into all the cases Arter handled throughout his career.

sentences.text: "It's quite outrageous - there will be women living now with trauma imposed by him on them." When Det Insp Jaysen Veeren tried to investigate Arter a decade ago, he says senior Met bosses tried to interfere with his work.

sentences.text: Alan Milburn's long-awaited plan to help young people who are neither learning nor earning promises to save money from the UK's welfare bill.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: Milburn said he believes his proposed reforms, which would reduce benefits for some young people who are not in education, employment or training (Neets) but aim to get them jobs in the long run, could save as much as £13.8bn in welfare costs over the next 10 years.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: But after the extra spending he has proposed for job guarantees from the government, hiring incentives for firms, and health and education support, his reforms are only projected to save £200m a year of taxpayers' money overall by 2036.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: BBC Verify has taken a look through the numbers.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: Burnham wants Neets report to be watershed moment, No 10 says, as Tories criticise welfare and tax proposals Analysts have expressed concerns about the sharply rising number of young people claiming health and disability benefits in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: The Milburn report estimates that around £8bn a year is currently being spent on benefits directly for young people through the welfare system, made up of £4.6bn on Universal Credit and £3.2bn on Personal independence payments (Pip).
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: The number of 16-24 year olds in England and Wales claiming the health element of Universal Credit has increased from 105,000 in 2020 to 193,000 this year according to the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP).
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: Young Pip claimants have also increased from 230,000 to 511,000 over that time, while official forecasts suggest this number is set to rise , external above 800,000 by 2037.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: He is also proposing a new benefits system so young people would not be able to access the same kind of health and disability benefits as older people, including creating a Youth Allowance instead of giving under-25s Universal Credit and a new Additional Cost Allowance that could replace Pip benefits.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: Milburn estimates that these reforms would contribute to a reduction of total welfare spending of £3.6bn a year by 2036 relative to where spending would otherwise have been in that year, and said it could save a cumulative £13.8bn from the welfare bill over the next decade.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: Milburn said his diagnosis applies UK-wide, but education, skills, health and local government are devolved to Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: He has called on the devolved administrations to agree "a shared set of headline outcomes".
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: Watch: What's in the Milburn review?
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: Official forecasts show the total welfare system , external is projected to cost £353bn this year.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: There is no official forecast of the level of total welfare spending in 2036, but likely inflation means it would be above the £431bn currently projected for 2032.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: Around half of this cost is the state pension, on which spending is forecast to rise from £154bn a year to £193bn a year.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: Spending on Pip and disability living allowance are also set to rise over that time from £40bn a year to £57bn a year.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: However, as a share of the overall economy, the increase in the cost of the welfare system is less dramatic.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: Total welfare spending is forecast to rise from 11.1% of GDP this year to 11.3% in 2032.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: This would be below the the peak of around 12% seen in 2013 following the global financial crisis.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: That has led some economists and researchers to question the argument , external that welfare spending is out of control.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: The reductions touted as part of Milburn's reforms, if delivered, would likely only reduce the UK's benefits bill by a relatively small amount.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: As a share of today's welfare bill, the £3.6bn of annual savings in 2036 would be only 1%.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: As well as the £5.8bn that would be spent on supporting young people into work, training or college, Milburn estimates the government would reap £2.4bn a year in additional taxes, as more people would be in work.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: This £2.4bn of additional taxes combined with the £3.6bn in lower welfare spending would add up to £6bn a year in 2036.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: That implies a net saving for the government as a result of Milburn's proposed package of £200m by that year, although this saving would grow over time.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: The £200m net savings figure in the Milburn report is also in today's money - and would be larger in cash terms in 2036, though the actual cash figure will depend on inflation over the next decade.
sentences.article_title: Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

sentences.text: Alan Milburn has said the country needs a "complete system reset" to bring down the number of young people not in work or education - known as "Neets".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: In a major review, published on Tuesday, , external he suggested a raft of proposals to address the problem, which mostly cover England but he says can be adapted in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland too.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Each of his recommendations will need to be accepted by the government and implemented and paid for before they become reality - and that could take some time.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: So how might today's proposals affect you if you are Neet?
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Major report proposes welfare changes, apprenticeships and tax cuts to help 440,000 young people into work At the heart of the recommendations, Milburn says, is a new Youth Opportunity Service.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He wants this to be implemented locally, with each area drawing up a plan to help their own young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: It would bring together employment, careers, health and practical support, with each young person getting a named adviser and a personalised plan.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants areas to begin building their Youth Opportunity Service from 2027, with one in place everywhere by the end of 2029.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within 14 days of entering the service, a young person would then meet with a named adviser.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within four weeks, they would have their "personalised participation plan", setting out what both the support services and the young person involved would do, and when.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Jobs wise, Milburn wants there to be initiatives like work placements of up to 12 weeks, structured volunteering opportunities, and help to create businesses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants those who remain Neet - despite enagaging with support - to be provided with a paid six-month job, funded by the government.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The government has already committed to a legal guarantee of job support in theory , but the exact workings still need to be worked out.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Alongside more work opportunities, Milburn wants a "major expansion" in further education for 18- to 24 year-olds, as well as more apprenticeship places.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Over the next decade, he wants the number of young people completing an apprenticeship to double, and for apprenticeships to rival university as an option for school leavers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Colleges should also get new funding for participation and work-readiness, the review says, initially targeted at 16- and 17-year-olds who are Neet or at serious risk of becoming so.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants the government to develop new industry-led technical colleges and specialist campuses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: If the reforms are enacted, Milburn says young people should have better access to high-quality further education and apprenticeships by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Under the proposals, schools, colleges and universities would be judged by whether pupils make successful transitions into further learning and work, rather than just academic achievements.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: By 2036, he wants 35% of each year group to have started a high-quality apprenticeship by age 25.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The young people caught up in Britain's Neets crisis At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report Milburn has said he wants a fundamental transformation of how mental health support for young people is delivered.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Young people who are Neet should be guaranteed fast-track access to services within three months, according to his recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: This would include things like vocational rehabilitation, talking therapies and counselling as part of a young person's plan with their local Youth Opportunity Service - which would be rolled out between 2027 and 2029 under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: There has been a big rise in mental distress among children and young people in recent years, and Milburn's report comes at a time the NHS is facing huge pressures.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants mental health support to be available for all young people digitally, without needing a diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Some areas are already using these approaches, but scaling them up would be a major challenge and would take a long time to introduce across the board.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Plus, Milburn wants "fitness to work" notes to be taken out of the hands of GPs and put into community work and health teams, and for them to be "a trigger for help - not simply a certificate of absence".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants these changes to begin in 2027 and would be linked to the Youth Opportunity Service rollout, which would be complete by 2029 under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn has said he wants companies to be incentivised to employ more young people, with the report highlighting a competitive jobs market and applicants who often fail to hear back from potential employers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The report includes three asks of employers: to create more genuine first jobs, more first-job apprenticeships and much wider access to meaningful work experience.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Plus, Milburn wants large employers to find ways of responding to rejected job applicants.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: These changes should be felt by both employers and the young people looking for jobs by 2029, the report says.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: To achieve this, the report suggests a £3,000 payment for employers who take on someone who has been Neet for six months, with a further premium of £2,000 available if they are a small business.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: An extra payment of £2,000 would go to employers taking on somebody taking substantially greater barriers, such as care leavers or disabled young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: These payments are proposed to be part of changes to the Youth Jobs Grant - which already exists , external - but they would expand under Milburn's proposals from 2027.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The E1 area east of Jerusalem is a strategically important part of the occupied West Bank The UK has sanctioned companies it said were involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
sentences.article_title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements

sentences.text: The government said the sanctions against eight construction and property development firms would disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support building in the West Bank.
sentences.article_title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements

sentences.text: Settlements are illegal under international law, and there has been a rise in violence towards Palestinians in the West Bank by settlers in recent months.
sentences.article_title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements

sentences.text: It comes two days before the deadline for bids for construction tenders in the E1 area east of Jerusalem.
sentences.article_title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements

sentences.text: The plans, which have been condemned internationally, would in effect divide the West Bank in two and isolate East Jerusalem.
sentences.article_title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements

sentences.article_title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements

sentences.article_title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements

sentences.article_title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements

sentences.text: Gloria Stephenson was killed while crossing a road in Sunderland in May last year The rider of an illegal e-motorbike who knocked down and killed an 86-year-old grandmother has had his "unduly lenient" jail term increased by almost two years.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: Billy Stokoe, then 18, had taken cannabis and was using a mobile phone when he hit Gloria Stephenson on a zebra crossing in Sunderland last year, then rode off.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: In May he admitted causing death by dangerous driving and was sentenced to six years and nine months but, after a referral by the solicitor general, judges at the Court of Appeal raised it to eight years and six months.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: Julie Francis, one of the victim's daughters, said the decision would not "bring our mum back" but "I feel like as a family we've been listened to".
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: Dashcam footage showed Stokoe did not slow down or try to avoid Stephenson, who was walking her daughter's dog and trying to complete her 10,000 steps a day.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: Stokoe was thrown off the motorbike but did not stop at the scene.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: Instead, he rode away to change his clothes and hide the bike at a friend's house before handing himself in at a police station just over an hour later.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: This video can not be played Warning: Contains distressing scenes.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: The barrister said the sentencing judge either used the wrong starting point for the sentence, did not increase the sentence enough because of the aggravating elements of the crime "or gave too much weight to the mitigation", making the sentence unduly lenient.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: Stokoe appeared at the appeal hearing via a link from HMP Deerbolt in County Durham.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: His barrister Helen Towers said he had been "glued to his phone" as he was riding the motorbike, but argued the sentencing judge at Newcastle Crown Court did not make a "gross error".
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: However, Lord Justice Stuart-Smith, sitting with Mrs Justice Farbey and Judge Mark Lucraft KC, said there should have been a "significant" uplift to the starting point of the sentence.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: Billy Stokoe admitted causing death by dangerous driving Stephenson, who was a mother to four daughters and had 13 grandchildren, had been widowed three times and enjoyed a successful career in the NHS.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: She was described by her family as having a "zest for life".
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: Julie Francis said she was relieved Stokoe's sentence had been increased and described her mother's death as "unimaginable".
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: Speaking outside court, she said: "No matter what sentence the judge passed, it's not going to bring our mum back.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: "[Stokoe] has taken her life, but I feel like as a family we've been listened to, our concerns have been listened to.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: "There were so many factors that contributed to this collision and it was inevitable that someone was going to be hurt.
sentences.article_title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased

sentences.text: The government is to change the law so that it no longer has to give failed asylum seekers notice before they are removed from the country.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: Currently, people are given five working days' notice but ministers believe this leads to last-minute appeals which delay the process.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: Under the new rules, once an asylum claim fails, the Home Office would have six months in which to remove the applicant without telling them in advance.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: The move was criticised by the Refugee Council which said: "Removing people at such short notice will cause unnecessary distress and anxiety to people." Imran Hussain, the director of the refugee charity, said: "The reality is that voluntary removals are far more effective at removing people than enforced returns.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: "If you assist people to return with dignity, many will take that option, at far lower cost to the taxpayer." Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood will make the change by amending the Immigration and Asylum Bill which is currently going through Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: The amendment will scrap the notice requirement for those who have exhausted the asylum appeals process.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: Instead, the Home Office will have the power to remove people immediately, a power that will remain in place for up to six months.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: The Home Office has not said how many additional people it thinks it will be able to remove but has pointed to Denmark where the number of migrants awaiting removal more than halved over five years to under 1,000 after a similar policy was introduced.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: The previous government, led by Sir Keir Starmer, had pledged to clear the asylum backlog.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: An asylum seeker is someone who wants to be in the UK because they say they cannot live safely in their own country due to persecution or violence.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: The government must house an asylum seeker if they cannot financially support themselves while their claim is being considered.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: There were 89,089 people in asylum accommodation as of June 2026.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: About 18% of those people, 16,021, were in hotels.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: These are used when there is not enough shared housing available, such as houses of multiple occupation (HMOs) or former military sites .
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: The government has pledged to stop the use of hotels by 2029.
sentences.article_title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period

sentences.text: More people are in hotels across the south of England than elsewhere in the UK, while HMOs are more common in the north of England and Scotland.

sentences.text: Louise, 30, says her addiction to decongestants left her feeling like a prisoner in her own body A woman says her blocked nose left her with a decade-long addiction to decongestant nasal sprays that cost her thousands.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: Louise Gough, 30, failed to read the fine print on her over-the-counter Sudafed which warns it is for short-term use only, and ended up addicted.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: She became so reliant on the medication she was spraying up to 15 times a day and felt like a "prisoner in her own body".
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: Sudafed said the safe use of its products was its top priority.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: But a consultant surgeon who treats this dependency said the warning should be more prominent on packaging.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: Gough, from Caerphilly, estimates she spent about £2,000, secretly buying bottles that cost about £7 because her partner was frustrated by her spending.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: "I used it [when I had a cold] and instantly within 10 seconds my nose was unblocked," she said.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: "The relief of that was phenomenal.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: I didn't read the box and I didn't realise that you could only use it for a certain amount in a time period.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: "No one ever warned me when I bought it.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: It just turned into a really vicious cycle." Prolonged use can make congestion worse, so even when Gough did not have a cold, her nose would be blocked and she would use the spray.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: She had developed rhinitis medicamentosa, a medication-induced nasal congestion also known as rebound congestion.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: "I found myself feeling really anxious if I didn't have a bottle on me," she said.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: "This was particularly bad if I was out with my partner as I'd ask him to get me one and he'd be annoyed.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: "I laugh about it now but it wasn't funny at the time.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: "I felt like a prisoner in my own body and I couldn't get away from it." Louise says she felt anxious when she did not have a nasal spray with her Ear, nose and throat (ENT) consultant Vik Veer said decongestant sprays work by temporarily restricting blood flow to the nasal lining.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: Prolonged use can trigger a cycle in which the nose becomes increasingly congested as the medication wears off.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: "The thing you were doing to try to make you better actually makes you even worse," he said.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: "Every ENT surgeon will know about [rebound congestion] and would see this problem almost in every clinic." Official recommendations are that nasal decongestant sprays , external containing xylometazoline and oxymetazoline should not be used for more than five consecutive days.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: But Veer said he believes rebound congestion can begin much sooner.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: "I think the evidence points towards you having problems within three days of using these sprays," he said.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: When Gough started taking decongestants, the recommendation was seven days, with the current five-day warning added to packaging in 2026.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: When Gough used two bottles in 11 days on her family holiday to Greece she said she knew she had to quit, and stopped taking them three years ago.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: "It's like someone has shoved something so far up your nose you physically can't breathe at all," she said.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: The first few days off the medication made her feel "claustrophobic in her own body" as she struggled to breathe naturally, she said.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: But after a month she was finally able to breathe through her nose unmedicated.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: But Gough has not regained her sense of taste and smell as strongly as before.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: A Sudafed spokesperson said its products followed strict regulatory and industry rules, with usage information provided on packaging, patient information leaflets and its website.
sentences.article_title: Woman who got hooked on nasal spray for 10 years says it cost her thousands

sentences.text: It encouraged anyone with questions about using its products to speak to a GP or pharmacist.

sentences.text: Russell Brand (pictured during his trial) delivered a message to followers via his wife Laura A message by Russell Brand to his followers in which he claimed innocence for his sexual offences was "clearly appalling" and is being urgently investigated, Downing Street has said.
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand prison message 'appalling' and being investigated, No 10 says

sentences.text: The comedian is currently serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand prison message 'appalling' and being investigated, No 10 says

sentences.text: His wife Laura read out a message from him on their Sunday Service show on YouTube, in which the convicted rapist claimed: "I am not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for." No 10 said it expects action to be taken if Brand is found to have broken prison rules.

sentences.article_title: Russell Brand prison message 'appalling' and being investigated, No 10 says

sentences.article_title: Russell Brand prison message 'appalling' and being investigated, No 10 says

sentences.text: "This is being urgently investigated, and I expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules." In the couple's podcast, released on Sunday, Laura Brand can be seen sitting on a sofa and is holding a Bible with a candle burning in front of her.

sentences.text: Relaying the message from her husband, Laura Brand said the comedian - who is currently being held at HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire - called prison staff "strong", "kind" and "dedicated", and asked people to support his "treasured wife and family".
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand prison message 'appalling' and being investigated, No 10 says

sentences.text: "Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments." Speaking earlier, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Sky News: "His crimes are heinous and awful.

sentences.text: A review by Alan Milburn (left) could create political headaches for Andy Burnham Andy Burnham has committed to bringing the welfare bill down, but he knows just how the high the political stakes are.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: He saw how last year's welfare rebellion marked the beginning of the end for his predecessor in Downing Street.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Sir Keir Starmer's authority was shredded when 120 - more than a quarter - of his own MPs threatened to derail his reforms.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: To defuse this, Sir Keir was compelled to guarantee that existing claimants of personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales, wouldn't lose out.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Even then, 49 of the 120 potential Labour rebels still voted against their own government.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Next week, a review from former New Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn has the capacity to create another internal row in Labour's ranks.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Milburn has spent a year grappling with how to reduce the nearly one million young people who are not in employment, education or training (Neets).
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: In an interview with the Times, he has now confirmed he is set to recommend cutting benefits for some 16-24 year olds who currently receive Pip, or the enhanced health-related payment of Universal Credit.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Taking benefit cuts to the Parliamentary Labour Party would usually have a similar effect to adding phosphorus to water.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But from my soundings, the deep waters of the Labour ranks are calmer than might be expected.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Importantly, two of the most effective organisers of last year's welfare rebellion are batting for the current prime minister, rather than against the previous one.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Louise Haigh is now the most powerful cabinet minister after Andy Burnham himself, while Anneliese Midgeley is his chief whip.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: And the MP who fronted that rebellion - Meg Hillier - has said she wants to give Milburn's proposals a "fair wind".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: There are also clear differences to the previous approach to welfare reform.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: First, it is not being presented as primarily a cost-cutting exercise with pre-determined savings.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Instead, there will be upfront investment to provide more support to unemployed young people, and a timeframe for net savings likely to be set at around a decade – gradualism, not a short, sharp shock.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Second, last year's initial reforms would have affected people in all age groups, whilst benefit cuts this time would be limited to the under 25s, who make up around 11% of Pip claimants.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say One in eight young people still out of work or education ahead of major review I've spoken to government ministers who had expressed concerns – at least privately – about the changes devised previously by Rachel Reeves and Liz Kendall.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: This time, they are on board.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: One of them told me that so long as there was enough support for young people, with guaranteed jobs and training, MPs would be "fine" with some benefit cuts.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But they added that it was vital that those who really couldn't work wouldn't be worse off.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Milburn will suggest there could even be enhanced payments for people in this category, while some young people with disabilities who lose out on Pip could nonetheless be given an additional "allowance" to help with living costs.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Another minister who opposed the previous reforms praised the process this time.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: There had been a high level of engagement not just from Milburn, but Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden, who has been taking MPs through the principles behind the reforms.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: One minister was a little more cautious, suggesting support for a reduction in benefits would depend on what the entire "package" of reforms looked like.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Milburn's recommendations are likely to be wide-ranging – from pre-school policies to how the NHS deals with mental health.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Some of the eventual 49 rebels from last year are in a similar place.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: York MP Rachael Maskell told me it was essential that she saw the detail of the proposals rather than the "drip, drip" of press reports which would "cause young people stress and distress".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: She felt withdrawing Pip from young people was "like a sledgehammer to crack a nut" and was concerned that some disabled people required it to remain in work.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: She also suggested that the government "shouldn't just point the finger at young people," and should look closely at how employers could take more youngsters on.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Stroud MP Simon Opher also voted against the government on welfare last year.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: He told me there was a "crisis" with so many Neets, and Milburn had come up with a "credible solution".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But he believes cutting benefits should be a "last resort" and is worried about restricting access to the health element of Universal Credit, as a quarter of young claimants aren't Neet.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: He concludes that the "devil will be in the detail".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: So much of politics - like comedy – depends on timing.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: For some sceptics, including serving ministers, the Milburn proposals will be more warmly welcomed if support for young people is in place before entitlements are withdrawn.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But for some Labour MPs, cutting payments to existing claimants crosses a line.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Clapham and Brixton Hill MP Bell Ribiero-Addy has she wasn't sure she could back cuts.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Referring to Pip, she didn't believe that "you get a disabled young person into work by taking away the money that helps them to get into work".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: And another MP on the left of the party, Brian Leishman, told the BBC he couldn't back benefits cuts as "we are in the middle of a cost of living crisis".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: So a welfare rebellion seems guaranteed if Burnham accepts Milburn's recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But it seems unlikely to be of the same scale, or have a similar level of political jeopardy to the one which shook the Starmer government.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: The government-commissioned work, led by former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn, is looking into how to solve the problem of nearly one million young people not being in employment, education or training, or Neet.

sentences.text: A key challenge is addressing the issue of school absence.

sentences.article_title: Children dropping out of school: What can politicians do about it?

sentences.text: A government spokesperson said: "When children feel they belong at school, they show up, and when they show up, they achieve." Therefore, the spokesperson added, "the education secretary is driving ambitious reforms to boost attendance" and "intervene earlier when children need support".

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrats also sought to pin the blame on the Tories.

sentences.text: She added that "every young person should feel they belong".
sentences.article_title: Children dropping out of school: What can politicians do about it?

sentences.text: These reactions prompt some of the big questions that arise from Eva and Mali's experiences.
sentences.article_title: Children dropping out of school: What can politicians do about it?

sentences.text: Where should responsibility for their situations lie?
sentences.article_title: Children dropping out of school: What can politicians do about it?

sentences.text: The individual, the parents, the rules in the pandemic, schools, colleges, mental health provision?
sentences.article_title: Children dropping out of school: What can politicians do about it?

sentences.text: Perhaps a combination of all of these things in some instances and other things besides.

sentences.article_title: Children dropping out of school: What can politicians do about it?

sentences.article_title: Children dropping out of school: What can politicians do about it?

sentences.text: "Schools are doing great work to bring absence down.
sentences.article_title: Children dropping out of school: What can politicians do about it?

sentences.text: Those children who have special education needs or are struggling to leave home, need specialist support and in some cases specialist schools." And she added: "High academic standards lift everyone up.

sentences.text: It is insulting to suggest that not all children are capable of good academic outcomes.

sentences.text: Sweeping reforms are needed to help 440,000 more young people into work, according to former minister Alan Milburn.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Almost one million young people aged 16 to 24 in the UK are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet" - a current rate of 13%, which Milburn wants to fall to around 5% within a decade.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: His government-commissioned review, due to be published in full on Tuesday, calls for ministers to intervene from early childhood through to adulthood, funded in part by radical changes to benefits for young adults.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: But Helen Whately, Conservative shadow work and pensions secretary, said Milburn's proposals were in parts "too cautious" and too reliant on the "expensive hand of the state".
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Many of the review's proposed changes are specific to England, with some welfare and tax measures applying across all home nations.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, says extensive change is needed to avoid a "lost generation", and address what he describes as a "moral" crisis.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: "We've got to get on with it, it's going to take time but I want to make sure every young person has a chance to earn or learn," he told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: The review says that, in 2024/25, for every £1 spent helping young people into work or education, £25 was spent on youth benefits.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: By 2036, it says the aim should be for that ratio to be £2 on benefits for every £1 on work support.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: "If we can get the benefits bill down, that is a good thing, but this is not about saving costs, it's about improving young people's lives," Milburn said.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: The service would put a young person in touch with a named adviser to help to secure them an apprenticeship, college place, supported employment or a job within four months.

sentences.text: The review's key welfare measures, some of which have already been announced , suggest replacing these benefits for under-25s with a new Youth Allowance at the current base rate of Universal Credit for young people, and a new Additional Cost Allowance to replace Pip.

sentences.text: Too many university students can use AI to complete assessments without staff finding out, the higher education regulator in England has said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The Office for Students (OfS) said "a significant proportion" of assessments are unsupervised and many can be completed to a high standard with AI, sometimes in minutes.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said this posed a "significant risk" to their credibility, and closed-book and practical exams were the most effective forms of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK said many institutions had "made substantial changes" to make assessments "AI-proof".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities that do not meet OfS quality standards could soon be banned from charging increased tuition fees or have caps imposed on their student numbers, under proposals that are now being consulted on.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The new research from the OfS and Advance HE, a charity that gives awards for teaching excellence, is based on the views of 244 higher education staff and 91 students from at least 127 universities.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said "a significant proportion of assessments" were in "unsupervised, non-controlled formats where AI can be accessed by students completing them".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "Many of these can be completed to a high standard using AI tools with limited engagement from students," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It also concluded it was "frequently possible" for students to use AI "in ways that cannot be reliably detected".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Unsupervised assessment can include coursework, but also remote online exams.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: They were rolled out widely during Covid, and research from Swansea University , external last year suggests 93 universities in the UK still use them in some form.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Josh Fleming, director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said there were "fantastic" examples of universities seizing opportunities presented by AI, but there should be "far greater use of AI-free assessment".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It also presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students' learning and institutions' ability to assess them," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Kathryn Harrison-Graves, deputy chief executive at Advance HE, said students wanted "greater clarity about what is expected of them" but staff had "varying levels of confidence and support".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Some staff, meanwhile, were receiving lots of assignments that looked the same, and did not think their institution's assessments were "fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Other staff described a "polarised atmosphere" between students who used AI and other "conscientious objectors" who avoided it on environmental and other grounds.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The research said AI literacy for students was important during and after university, and some institutions were clearly communicating to students where AI can and cannot be used in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: But it said there was "an urgent need" to ensure that remote or "non-secure" assessments "maintain their validity despite the availability of AI tools, meaning they effectively assess the knowledge and skills they are designed to measure".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "If it becomes possible to complete an assessment using AI without the knowledge and skills being tested, the assessment should be replaced," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK, which represents more than 140 institutions, said universities were "making significant progress" adapting to AI.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "There is further to go but many have made substantial changes to how they assess students.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: This includes more in-person exams, presentations, vivas, process-based assessment and assessments that integrate AI in a controlled way," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It's time to get rid of the outdated methods, that have been kept around in the name of tradition, and instead encourage the innovative practice we see across the sector, co-designed with students based on what they want from higher education," he said.

sentences.text: The government has warned some schools start teaching GCSEs in the first year of secondary school Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught in England.

sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: A single meteor streaks across the starry night sky during the annual Leonid meteor shower The Leonid meteor shower reaches its peak on Tuesday night, giving UK sky gazers their best chance to see it this year.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: The celestial spectacle runs until 30 November, but the greatest activity is expected on the night of Tuesday 17 November, into the early hours of Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: There could be the chance to spot up to 10-15 meteors per hour.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: The shower is made up of dust particles from the Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which leaves a trail of debris as it follows its path around the Sun.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: These particles enter the Earth's atmosphere at up to 44 miles (71km) per second, meaning these streaks of light are the fastest meteors in the sky.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: Experts advise finding a safe, dark location away from sources of light pollution such as street lights.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: The meteors will be visible with the naked eye, with no binoculars or telescope required.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: However, giving your eyes some time to adapt to the dark, perhaps 20 or 30 minutes, will give you the best chance of spotting them.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: A wide open space is the best place to be, giving a full view of the night sky.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: Meteors could be visible anywhere but the Leonids' radiant, the point from which they seem to appear, will, as the name suggests, be around the head of the constellation Leo, meaning this is the best part of the sky to focus your gaze.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: Leo does not rise until around midnight, so the best time to look is after midnight and in the hours before dawn.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: As with all celestial spectacles, clear skies will be a must.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: Plants and trees from hotter parts of the world are being brought into Sussex Gardeners in one of the most drought-hit parts of the UK have said they are adapting their planting strategies amid increasingly extreme weather.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: West Sussex - like most of the country - experienced an unprecedented summer marked by record-breaking heatwaves and severe drought.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: The conditions have put immense stress on many traditional plant species, with some seriously struggling or dying completely.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Iain Parkinson, head of landscape and horticulture at Kew Wakehurst near Ardingly, said he had seen a "big change" in climate over the some 40 years he has worked there.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: "We've had trees die," he added.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Meanwhile, senior gardener at High Beeches near Haywards Heath, Elliot Chandler, said some rhododendrons had died off this year.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: "That's probably going to continue," he said.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: "We'll do what we can for the plants...but if they're not surviving, then we need to plant different things.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: "That's the only way we can really maintain the garden and keep it full of interest and flowers." This year's heat and lack of rainfall were unprecedented Joe Whelan, head gardener at Nymans in Handcross, warned another year of drought could be "quite detrimental" on larger, more mature trees.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: The gardeners said planting a greater diversity of species will be key to climate resilience, with plants from North America, southeastern Europe, central Asia, South Korea and Japan potentially faring better in future.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Chandler added it will not be a case of ripping out old plants and planting new species "in one go" but rather a gradual change over time with a "really diverse mix of things".
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Whelan said it will be difficult to predict what will do well in the future.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: It will be about "experimenting and accepting that some things probably aren't going to make it", he continued.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Lydia Dibben wants more small farms around Wales growing produce Droughts and wildfires in the summer were a wake-up call, and winter flooding could leave Wales' food supply vulnerable, an expert has warned.

sentences.text: The country currently imports the vast majority of its fruit and vegetables, with only 6% of those served in its schools grown in Wales.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: It is dependent on produce from parts of the world prone to droughts and fires, according to co-founder of an organisation aiming to address this.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Duncan Fisher is behind Our Food Trust , external , which wants to build 100 farms, producing fruit and vegetables in Wales for local markets.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Despite 90% of the country being used for agriculture , external , only about 0.1% is currently being used for horticulture , external .
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Growers at Fisher's Wern Farm, near Newtown, Powys, said this must change if the country is to survive climate change, wars and other global disruptions to the supply chain.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "We are hugely dependent and these vegetables are coming from really vulnerable parts of the world like south Europe and north Africa - the areas most prone to drought, fires and overheating," said Fisher.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Food security has become a hot topic , with Defence Secretary Wes Streeting saying in October people should have water, tinned goods, baby food, torches and mobile phone charging packs ready in case of emergency.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: Fisher referenced this appeal, adding the UK "has an incredibly centralised food system with 95% of the food we eat bought from nine supermarkets".
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: He said: "There's no storage, it's a just-in-time system so the food is stored in lorries moving across motorways.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "That is a security hazard because it's very vulnerable to cyber-attacks.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: "If the system goes wrong, there's no resilience in it.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: The food just runs out straight away." Duncan Fisher said he has hope that Wales will be able to increase its fruit and veg growing Fisher and Sue Holbrook launched Our Food Trust about 10 years ago with the aim of growing more produce locally for local markets.

sentences.text: They found one of the main barriers was stable housing for farmers.
sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: As Fisher explained: "If there's a high wind during the night, they need to get out there and protect things.

sentences.article_title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies

sentences.text: The world's largest LGBTQ+ dating app, Grindr, has defended its $120 (£91) per month premium subscription service, which launches globally today.
